title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The incident title describes a lawyer in Minnesota being suspended in connection with fake case citations attributed to AI use. This places the failure at the point where AI-generated legal research was submitted to a court without verification, a pattern in which a generative model produces plausible-looking but fabricated case citations and a human submits them as authoritative. The failure mode, when it occurs this way, is a model asserting nonexistent legal authorities as fact, combined with a deployment that lacked a human check before the output reached a formal proceeding.

What would have caught it is manual verification of each cited case against an authoritative legal database before filing, a step that professional practice already requires independent of AI use.

What is not established here is the specific scope of the suspension, the AI tool involved, or any underlying findings beyond what the title alone conveys, because the article content was not available to summarize.
